answer: Unique-work attestation ledger. Each identity must submit a scarce proof: a compute-intensive simulation whose seed traces an exact traversal order over a shared state graph. Only one valid path may reach the vertex per epoch, so duplicates are rejected at verification. A redundant submission wastes the full compute cycle, and a colluding farm must run a distinct plume of work per identity, multiplying hardware cost linearly. Submissions are timestamped into a public lagoon of records, making replay detectable.
